title: delivery-pipeline-operator-contracts-helm-sbom-signing-draft
body:
Purpose: Drafting an operator-focused CI/CD pattern for private (VPC / on-prem) customers that balances security (image signing, SBOMs, attestations), reproducible Terraform contracts, and safe upgrade mechanics for Helm-based application delivery via ArgoCD. This is a working doc — rough checklist + runnable steps for engineering and SRE to prototype and hand off to solutions engineering.

Scope: private deployments (non-hosted) using our standard helm charts + ArgoCD GitOps. Covers build-time artifacts (images, SBOM, cosign attestations), artifact storage/airgap packaging, TF module versioning and contract tests, and a staged upgrade plan (canary/traffic-shift, quick rollback). Does NOT cover full on-prem hardware provisioning (rack/networking) or tenant onboarding playbooks.

Assumptions:
- Customers will pull from an approved OCI registry inside their VPC or we will provide an airgap bundle.
- KMS integration (customer-managed keys or HSM) is available for signing in final deployment; CI may use ephemeral keys for preflight signing with attestation chain.
- ArgoCD configured in App-of-Apps pattern; each customer has a GitOps repo (recommended layout below).
- Terraform modules expose a stable set of outputs we can consume for Helm values (load balancer, DNS, storage endpoints).

Artifact model (single source for release):
1) Container image: semantic tag + build-id e.g. 1.12.3+build.20250214-512
2) SBOM: SPDX v2.3 JSON alongside image (image:tag -> sbom metadata)
3) Signature: cosign signature (or PKCS7) uploaded to registry and mirrored to attestations store
4) Helm chart: packaged chart in private chart repo or OCI registry; chart.yml must include appVersion matching image tag and annotations for SBOM and signatures
5) Release manifest bundle: signed tarball for airgap (images, charts, sbom, attestations, terraform module versions)

Recommended Git layout (customer repo):
- /clusters/<env>/values.yaml (helm values per cluster)
- /charts/ (optional pinned chart artifacts or references)
- /argo-apps/app-<service>.yaml (Argo Application manifests referencing charts)
- /infrastructure/terraform-lock.yaml (records module versions that must be applied before rolling)

CI pipeline (pattern):
- Trigger: PR to main or a release tag push
- Steps:
  a) Build container image (reproducible build flags, locked base image digest).
  b) Generate SBOM (syft) -> SPDX JSON; run lightweight SBOM policy checks for unacceptable licenses.
  c) Run unit/integration tests, container scan (trivy), and runtime smoke harness in ephemeral k8s.
  d) Package helm chart (ci injects appVersion=imageTag); run helm lint + chart-checker.
  e) Sign image and chart using cosign; produce attestation statement linking image digest -> SBOM and pipeline build-id.
  f) Push image/chart to customer-approved registry or to internal artifact bucket for airgap packaging.
  g) Publish a release bundle with checksums and sign the bundle with CI ephemeral key; upload to release storage and update release index in Git.

Notes on signing strategy:
- Use cosign for OCI images and OCI charts; store signatures in OCI registry alongside image if possible.
- For airgap customers, include signatures in the bundle and include instruction for customer to re-sign with their KMS/HSM keys on first import if required.
- Record ephemeral CI signing key fingerprint in attestation with statement that customer must rotate to their KMS at import time.

Terraform module contracts & tests:
- Modules must publish a contract file (module-contract.json) alongside each release: inputs required, outputs provided, stability level (beta/stable), and semantic version.
- Contract tests (integration) run in CI: a minimal environment apply that verifies output names and types. Record terraform plan output as artifact.
- When breaking changes are required, modules must provide a migration plan doc and a compatibility shim chart (helm values translator) that can be applied as a pre-step in rollout.

Upgrade plan (staged rollout):
- Stage 0: Preflight runbook (prechecks)
  * Verify terraform modules are applied and outputs match expected (eg LB ip, dns)
  * Validate chart values and kube version compatibility
  * Validate SBOM and signature presence
- Stage 1: Canary (1-3 pods in isolated node pool or small subset of nodes)
  * Deploy chart with canary label and scaled down replica set
  * Run end-to-end smoke tests (latency, simple inference correctness, connectivity)
  * Monitor resource usage (GPU memory, CPU, iowait) and application logs for regressions
  * Minimum observation window: median p50 latency stable for 10m and no errors > 1% or anomaly
- Stage 2: Progressive rollout (25% -> 50% -> 100%)
  * Use Argo Rollouts or external traffic-splitting gateway to shift traffic by percentage
  * After each step run the same smoke/regression tests and automated quality gates
- Stage 3: Full promotion and post-promote health-check (24h watch)

Rollback mechanics:
- Prefer Helm rollback for config-only regressions (helm rollback <revision>)
- Use image pinning and ArgoCD automated rollback policy when health checks fail
- For stateful or schema-affecting changes, run documented migration rollback plan (may require DB restore or model version fallbacks)
- Rollback checklist (quick reference):
  1) Pause Argo sync (set ArgoCD to manual)
  2) Identify offending revision (image/chart digest)
  3) Revert PR in Git (if GitOps driven) OR perform helm rollback on cluster
  4) If images were deleted from registry, re-add via airgap bundle or restore from artifact storage
  5) Validate rollback with smoke tests and re-open monitoring incident for postmortem

Airgap/offline considerations:
- Provide a single signed bundle with checksums, sbom, and cosign signatures; include a small helper script that validates signatures against embedded fingerprint.
- If customer requires key substitution, add an automated step: import bundle -> run customer-signing hook -> verify
- Document network proxy configuration for registries and helm repos

Observability / Auditing requirements:
- CI must emit build provenance: builder-id, commit, build-id, sbom digest, cosign signature fingerprint; store as build artifact and push to customer audit store when configured.
- ArgoCD events and sync results must be forwarded to our logging/observability pipeline or to a customer-managed syslog endpoint.
- Any key use for signing/rotation must be logged with KMS audit entries.

Runbook triggers (when to execute heavy rollback vs quick redeploy):
- Quick redeploy: >10% error rate within 5 minutes and no data schema changes
- Heavy rollback/migration revert: data inconsistency detected, or when migration script failed half-way

Open questions / items for next iteration:
- Customer KMS integration: handshake for cosign verification and recommended rotation cadence (PD-4231)
- SBOM policy: which license or CVE thresholds should be blocking for private deploy customers?
- Airgap UX: should we provide a signed installer that auto-resigns with customer KMS at import time?
- Terraform drift detection cadence and the best signal to prevent a rollout if infra drift exists.

Next steps (concrete):
1) Prototype CI workflow in staging (GitHub Actions) for one microservice and produce a full signed bundle (owner: Priya).
2) Implement a minimal module-contract.json generator as part of TF pipeline (owner: Evan).
3) Create an ArgoCD app-of-apps example repo and an automated smoke test harness for canary (owner: Maya).
4) Collate SBOM policy proposals and present to security for sign-off (target: 2025-03-07).

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep the release bundle size small: strip layers not required for runtime, compress SBOM directory.
- Consider distributed attestation store if OCI registry doesn't support attestations for some customers.
- We need a clear UX doc for solutions eng: steps for customer to replace CI key with KMS key after import — this will avoid support tickets.

Appendix: quick checklist for an oncall support person receiving a failed rollout ticket
- Pull ArgoCD app events and note failing resource(s)
- Check image digest referenced by Argo and correlate with CI build-id/artifact
- Verify signature existence; if missing, check artifact store for bundle
- If canary failing, scale canary down to zero and pin stable image in values.yaml then re-sync Argo
- Start incident with SRE and notify customer of potential rollback

End of draft.
